title: DataRunner: complete customer-owned recurring SQL reporting and independent delivery handover

task.name: Deliver the selected customer report from its approved SQL source on the customer's actual reporting calendar
task.purpose: Give the selected consultancy and its customer a maintained reporting operation: the agreed complete query result, readable files or existing destination update, a usable schedule, retained delivery history and an independently operated handover. Keep the consultancy's data model, transformations and BI presentation with their current owners.
task.request: Continue the original customer workshare and selected Installation. Bind one actual customer-owned DataRunner workspace, its supported SQL connection, saved query and complete report definition. Preserve the current SQL version, parameters, source population, expected row count, decimal/key/null/time meanings, and any upstream Python or warehouse transformation. Select the actual useful report period, timezone, business calendar, recipients and delivery route. First run the complete approved report, review the actual output and native run/delivery history, and receive those complete files into the existing source workspace. Save the accepted schedule in DataRunner's original console. Operate the next genuinely due period, compare source and query changes, and resolve an included corrected-source or query revision through the same original report. Independently reopen the complete handover and have the named receiving operator execute the documented original workflow.
task.completeOutput: The original customer scope and source authority; actual workspace/connection/query/report/schedule/channel identities and operator ownership; complete reviewed SQL with parameter and timezone definitions; retained complete CSV/XLSX/PDF or selected destination output, exact source/run/delivery histories, row/column/completeness review, baseline and due-period comparison, any corrected source/query edition and its resolution; full existing source-workspace export plus configuration/runbook, original customer workshare, receiving results and operator handover. Private credentials remain in their existing credential store.
task.repeatTrigger: A customer-selected reporting period or an actual source/query change creates a useful new result when the agreed business decision requires it. The named operator selects daily, weekday, weekly or another actual cadence from that need. A channel retry, recovered run, repeat download, SQL reread, empty-result alert suppression or reopening the same retained result continues its original report operation. A corrected result preserves the predecessor and follows the original correction scope.
task.pricedUnit: Retain the original customer implementation and ongoing-reporting agreement separately from DataRunner's subscription. If the report consumes an approved paid Stellar source, use that merchant's complete useful source/result unit, actual atomic terms and original buyer authority; keep separately charged underlying requests together with the complete report they support. Subscription, implementation, ongoing support and paid-source purchases retain their own original billing units and terms.

source.reference: The selected customer's complete approved SQL report, current supported database or retained complete source export, actual DataRunner workspace/query/report/schedule/run and delivery identities, original query version, parameters, timezone and report period. Product and provider contract: DATARUNNER_REPORTING.md alongside this maintained profile; https://www.datarunner.app/en/docs/getting-started and https://www.datarunner.app/en/docs/reports.
source.population: Every row and column required by the selected report and its original query parameters and reporting window. Retain the complete raw file/result, original row and column counts, effective query/connection/version and any source scope restriction. Preserve full predecessor and successor editions for comparison. Where the approved output is an aggregate, retain its actual aggregation definition and complete result rather than inventing underlying source rows.
source.meaning: Retain original SQL aliases and physical column meanings, stable business keys, exact integers/decimals, unit/currency, original null and empty-string behavior, timestamp types and explicit reporting timezone, and inclusive/exclusive parameter bounds. Preserve upstream transformations, query definitions and data masking. A CSV export must have an explicitly reviewed complete header/type/null mapping; keep original bytes and query/version context before preparing the existing dataset engine.
source.changePolicy: Review database/schema, query/version, parameter, timezone, recipient, delivery and masking changes against the previous selected report. The customer approves the complete successor before its original schedule changes; preserve the previous source/result and review. Correct the original failed or inaccurate period through its existing operation and record why it was changed. Further databases, transformations, reports, recipients, operating periods or support obligations follow the original workshare.

receiving.application: DataRunner's original customer-owned console and, when its actual account includes API keys, the official pinned DataRunner CLI. Receive complete approved source/result files through the existing maintained source workspace and Installation desk. Optional paid-source publication uses the original SF30 dataset configuration, seller and buyer workflow after its exact dataset and payment selections are reviewed.
receiving.acceptanceRule: The named operator opens the actual saved report and complete source definition, runs the selected period through the original console/CLI, reviews all output rows and fields and actual completion state, opens every agreed file or destination output, and reconciles its native delivery route history. Save the useful customer calendar with an explicit timezone, then receive and review a genuinely due later period. Preserve and resolve a corrected source/query edition through the original operation. Independently receive the complete source workspace and operator package, reopen the real outputs and retained history, and complete an operator-led continuation of that same reporting workflow.
receiving.changeAndWithdraw: The customer owns source rights, database access, DataRunner account and report recipients. The consultancy owns its agreed SQL/model/transformation work and handover. The operator owns the selected schedule and destination configuration. Keep withdrawn routes and changed reports in original history; remove or pause the actual schedule when the customer withdraws the recurring task and update its existing operational record.
receiving.recovery: Read the original run and delivery history before any retry. Retain the same report/query/run and route identities, original result files and last accepted edition. Reopen a completed result instead of executing its query again merely to recover a download. For signed generic webhooks verify the original raw-body signature and deduplicate on the actual run plus route; distinguish a provider test probe from a complete report. Recover the existing source workspace and original receiving selection after interruption, preserving completed route outcomes.
receiving.maintenance: Name the customer account owner, SQL/transformation maintainer, database administrator, schedule operator, recipient/destination owner, source payer and independent receiving operator. Retain the exact selected DataRunner plan and CLI version, original key scope and secret-store reference, timezone/calendar, report-size and retention limits, failure route, business support window and change/withdrawal procedure. Review actual run duration, complete rows, delivery failures and operator effort with the customer at its agreed interval.

steps.title: Bind the original customer report and recurring job
steps.result: Receive the complete original customer scope and current Workshare/Installation. Select the actual report audience, decision, source database, query owner, current delivery-maintenance need, whole output and useful reporting calendar. The customer implementation and ongoing operation retain their own agreed scope, commercial owner and terms.

steps.title: Select the actual workspace and supported connection
steps.result: Use the customer-owned DataRunner console, original workspace and actual account plan. Confirm the selected database provides query support and the deployment permits that connection. Retain source-use authority, credential-store reference, schema/version and operator roles. On API/CLI installations receive the official binary/version and scopes actually exposed by that account.

steps.title: Review the complete SQL and source meanings
steps.result: Open the saved original query and version. Retain parameter values and reporting window, source keys, exact values, nulls, units and timezone. Keep upstream Python/warehouse transformations with their current owners. Review the complete result and its actual row count and size before scheduling; retain the original source and the complete agreed file output.

steps.title: Commission the actual report and destination
steps.result: Select CSV, XLSX, PDF or inline output according to the agreed customer use. Configure the existing email, signed webhook, Sheets or other documented destination and its actual recipients. Test its configuration, then run the complete report and inspect the real route history and delivered output. Retain the actual report, run and destination identities.

steps.title: Operate the useful reporting calendar
steps.result: Save the report's own cron/timezone and agreed weekdays, holidays or reporting periods in the original console. Set its selected empty-result and threshold behavior and failure notification. Complete the first baseline and a genuinely due later reporting period, comparing source freshness, full result, recipient resolution and delivery outcomes. Retain measured operator effort and useful task identities.

steps.title: Receive complete source editions and optional paid-source handoff
steps.result: Retain the complete source/result bytes and original run context in the existing source workspace. Review every column and null/type decision before using the maintained SF30 CSV dataset path; inspect its complete row count and retained snapshot. Any merchant publication and original buyer acquisition use the selected source rights, atomic terms and accountable deployments from the existing operating case.

steps.title: Correct a source or query change through the original report
steps.result: Preserve the accepted baseline and actual affected period, review the changed source/query/parameters or destination, and save the approved successor with its original reason and owner. Operate the corrected report, compare complete outputs and reconcile the original route history. Keep correction scope and any new useful task charge as recorded by the original agreement.

steps.title: Independently receive and hand over the complete operation
steps.result: Export the whole existing source workspace and the actual non-secret report/connection/query/schedule/destination definitions, complete results/history and operating guide. Receive them into the named independent location, reopen the real output and original operation context, and complete the selected workflow with the receiving operator. Hand over account, database, report, destination, source and ongoing-support ownership in the original case.

inputs: Complete original customer Workshare/Installation selection and agreed implementation, recurrence, correction and support terms; preserve the original customer case and commercial owner
Actual customer-owned DataRunner account/workspace, supported query connection, source/database/hosting rights, query/model/transformation owner and current scheduler
Complete approved SQL text and saved version, actual parameters and reporting windows, timezone/calendar, source population and row-count/completeness expectations
Full column/key/null/decimal/unit/currency/timestamp meanings, original source files or live-source reference, complete result files and actual source/query/run identities
Actual report, schedule and channel/destination definitions, recipients and ownership, empty-result/threshold behavior and original run/delivery history
Selected account plan, installed official CLI version and current help/OpenAPI when using automation, actual key-scope/secret-store references and environment owner
Existing source workspace and maintained release, selected full CSV dataset/type/null mapping when used, whole workspace archive and original independent receiving location
Named reporting operator, source payer, database/SQL maintainer, customer reviewer, receiving engineer, handover dates and agreed ongoing support calendar
Actual paid-source selections when used: original merchant/buyer deployments, useful source/result unit, network/asset/recipient, atomic amount and full task budget
